newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen off $0.50-$1 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen off $0.50-$1 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Wednesday were seen falling another $0.50 to $1.00 per cwt amid further pressure from abundant numbers of hogs held back by last week's brutally cold weather, dealers said.
Dealers said it would probably take at least through Wednesday to get through the remainder of hogs delayed by recent poor weather.

Top prices for hogs delivered to the plant in Iowa and southern Minnesota were expected to range from $50.50 to $52.00. Tuesday's top was quoted at $52.50, according to USDA. Tuesday's top in Iowa was down $3.00 from Friday.

Illinois top hog prices at plants could range from $50.00 to $50.50. Indiana/Ohio top prices were seen at $49.50 to $50.50, sources there said. Demand Tuesday was light, with some buyers out of the market following active movement on Monday which had supplied more than enough hogs.
Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hog receipts Monday totalled 126,000 head, above the estimate of 120,000, USDA said. Tuesday's estimated receipts were 115,000 head.

Weak pork prices also weighed on cash hog values, dealers said. Fresh pork bellies at midday were quoted $2.00 per cwt lower and heavy hams were off $1.00-$2.00, USDA said. Loins were not quoted, but had a weaker undertone.
